This is a digital painting I made a few years ago.

I love your color usage. Is it supposed to be underwater? To me it feels like it is without any context.

Any chance you want to expand on your process? Do you start with a sketch? do you start all digital?
My thoughts exactly. Although there's that bit of an unreal element as well. Super intriguing. And I'm interested about the process as well. Would be super cool if you could share, OP. :)

At first it was not intended to be underwater. But I played up the atmospheric effects so much it eventually looked like it was underwater, so I then added the jelly fish guys to push it further. The process here started with blocking out the repetitive shapes (the stone monolith things) to create a sense of perspective and distance. This is a standard trick used in landscape concept art to convey space--repetition and variation. Repeat shapes and change scale to make space. If I remember correctly the monoliths came from a sketch page I made of various rock formations. The whole piece was started digitally while I referenced my sketchbook. I also referenced macro camera shots of moss that I took for the various flora. As far as tools; the entire peace was painted on a Cintique screen in Photoshop.

Thanks for the interest guys. You're inspiring me to illustrate more landscapes again--it's been a while.
Your painting style is so smooth, and your use of shading is awesome. Those mysterious jellyfish-like creatures near the top also look super cool. Are you an artist professionally, or...?

I got a BFA in Illustration. But I work as a video game and motion graphics artist. I never could earn money consistantly enough through freelance illustration. I wish I could land a concept artist gig.

Ooh, I was actually going to mention that the piece looked a lot like video game art, but I wasn't sure if it would be related at all, haha. On first glance it reminded me of TF2's sort of art style. And a concept artist is pretty awesome, too. Not something I could do, for sure. Keep up the great work. :)
I prefer to paint and sketch than working in 3d. Blender is not bad though.
